title: Learn from my mistake
text:
Learn from my mistake. Don't do it! Read all of the innumerable other reviews regarding the defective doorlatches on Panasonic residential microwave ovens. The Internet is literally clogged with bad reviews relating to this issue. And when the doorlatch fails, the oven is inoperable, period. You will find those reviews not only on Amazon but also on many other websites, including Panasonic's own website. On my first Panasonic residential model, the Prestige Genius model here, the doorlatch failed after 16 months. On my second Panasonic (identical) residential model, the doorlatch failed in only four months. To get a sense of the extent of the problem, simply google the following phrase: "Panasonic microwave door latch."

Panasonic residential-level microwave ovens are a good choice only if you want to replace your oven frequently. All of the very wonderful features of this oven end up meaning nothing, because the door latch is junky and destined to fail early. (Planned obsolescence?)

After spending hours researching other residential microwave brands and finding other serious problems relating to durability, and after learning that literally 50% of residential microwaves, regardless of the brand, are made in just one factory in China -- with virtually identical or identical internal parts -- I have moved on to commercial grade. The ordinary pull handle on most commercial models is much more reliable than a push-button system. A commercial grade microwave will not have all of the bells and whistles of a residential model, but it will be built for durability, and you can get a good one for $250 - 325.

After numerous bad experiences with residential models failing way too soon, durability is all I care about at this point.
